title: Rome's distinction: absolute prayer to God, relative prayer to the saints as intercessors
source_text: XC. Respondent Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae Orationem illam quam Scriptura proponit, ut partem cultus qui Deo proprius est, esse orationem absolutam, qua rogatur aliquis, ut ipse bonorum author atque largitor; non autem relativam, qua rogamus aliquem ut Deum pro nobis oret, & ea quibus egemus nobis a Deo impetret: se vero Angelos & Sanctos invocare non ut ipsos bonorum authores; sed solum ut eorundem bonorum impetratores, & nostros apud Deum intercessores: adeoque se non aliud ab Angelis & Sanctis petere quam ut Deum pro nobis orent: quemadmodum absque ulla in Deum injuria, rogamus ipsos fideles nobiscum in terra viventes, ut nos apud Deum precibus suis juvent.
pass_a_gloss: The Doctors of the Roman Church answer that the Prayer which Scripture sets forth as part of the worship which is proper to God is absolute prayer, by which someone is asked as himself the author and giver of goods; not however relative, by which we ask someone that he pray to God for us, and obtain for us from God the things we need: but that they invoke Angels and Saints not as themselves authors of goods; but only as obtainers of those same goods, and our intercessors with God: and so they ask nothing else of Angels and Saints than that they pray to God for us: just as, without any injury to God, we ask the faithful themselves living with us on earth to help us with God by their prayers.
pass_b_english: The teachers of the Roman Church reply that the prayer Scripture sets forth as part of the worship proper to God is absolute prayer, by which someone is asked as himself the author and giver of good things. It is not relative prayer, by which we ask someone to pray to God for us and obtain from God what we need.

They say they call on angels and saints not as authors of good things but only as those who obtain them for us, our intercessors with God. So they ask nothing more of angels and saints than that they pray to God for us, just as, without any wrong to God, we ask our fellow believers who live with us on earth to help us before God with their prayers.

lemmas.gloss: obtainers, those who secure by asking

choices.why: The scholastic term is kept and explained in the same sentence.
